objective.statement: Add rate limiting to the login endpoint of this Express API using a reusable middleware factory.
objective.success_definition: The login route is rate limited by IP with a reusable express-rate-limit middleware factory configured for windowMs 900000 and max 5; exceeded requests return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header and JSON error body; no global or other-route rate limiting, default in-memory store is used, and existing route handlers/business logic are not modified.

goals.statement: Create a reusable rate-limit middleware factory for additional endpoints.
acceptance: A middleware file (e.g., middleware/rateLimiter.js) exports a factory function.
The factory accepts { windowMs, max } as parameters.
The factory returns a configured rateLimit() instance with a custom handler.
The factory can be reused for additional endpoints with different configurations.

goals.statement: Apply rate limiting only to the login route.
acceptance: The middleware is applied to the login route (e.g., POST /login or POST /api/auth/login).
The middleware is not applied globally or to other routes unless asked.

goals.statement: Return HTTP 429 with Retry-After and JSON when the limit is exceeded.
acceptance: The response includes a Retry-After header with seconds until the window resets.
The JSON response body is { "error": "Too many requests", "retryAfter": <seconds> }.
The rate limiter uses the client IP address as the identifying key.
The project dependency list includes express-rate-limit.

goals.statement: Configure the login route with the stated defaults.

acceptance: No Redis or external dependency is used for rate-limit storage.

goals.statement: Avoid modifying existing route handlers or business logic.
acceptance: Changes are limited to adding the middleware factory, wiring it to the login route, and installing the dependency.
Existing route handler code and business logic remain unchanged.

constraints.statement: Apply rate limiting only to the login route, not globally or to other routes unless asked.
Use the default in-memory store (no Redis or external dependencies).
Do not modify existing route handlers or business logic.
Keep the code minimal — no comments beyond what's necessary to explain non-obvious lines.

non_goals.statement: Do not apply rate limiting globally.
Do not apply rate limiting to other routes unless asked.
Do not use Redis or external dependencies for rate-limit storage.
Do not modify existing route handlers or business logic.
Do not add rate limiting to additional endpoints now; only make the factory reusable for later.

include: The existing Express login route (e.g., POST /login or POST /api/auth/login).
A reusable rate-limit middleware factory file (e.g., middleware/rateLimiter.js).
App/router wiring that applies the factory to the login route with windowMs 900000 and max 5.
exclude: Existing route handlers and business logic.

assumptions.statement: The login route is one of the provided examples or is otherwise identifiable in the Express API.
The middleware factory can be created at middleware/rateLimiter.js or an equivalent conventional middleware path.
express-rate-limit's default IP-based keying can identify clients by IP address.
Adding middleware in the app/router is not considered modifying existing route handlers or business logic.
Retry-After should report the remaining seconds until the current rate-limit window resets.
The default in-memory store means express-rate-limit's built-in MemoryStore.

open_questions.question: Which exact login route path and file should receive the rate-limit middleware?
What middleware file path and name should be used if middleware/rateLimiter.js is not suitable?

verification.spec: Inspect package.json for the express-rate-limit dependency.
Review the middleware factory file for an exported function accepting { windowMs, max } and returning a configured rateLimit() instance with a custom handler.
verification.expected: The factory matches the stated parameters and returns a rateLimit instance with a custom handler.

verification.spec: Send 6 POST requests to the login route from the same IP within 15 minutes.
verification.expected: The first 5 requests are not rate-limited; the 6th returns HTTP 429.

verification.spec: Inspect the 429 response headers and body from the exceeded request.
verification.expected: The response includes a Retry-After header in seconds and JSON body { "error": "Too many requests", "retryAfter": <seconds> }.

verification.spec: Review app/router wiring to confirm the middleware is applied only to the login route.
verification.expected: No global rateLimit middleware or other-route rateLimit middleware is added.

verification.spec: Review the rate-limit configuration and imports for storage.
verification.expected: The default in-memory store is used; no Redis or external dependency is configured.

verification.spec: Review the diff for changes to existing route handlers or business logic.
verification.expected: Only the middleware factory, login route wiring, and dependency files change.

deliverables.description: Middleware factory file exporting a rate-limit factory configured with custom 429 handling.
Login route wiring that applies the factory with windowMs 900000 and max 5.

factors: The change affects the login endpoint.
The implementation adds an external package dependency.
The behavior changes when the rate limit is exceeded.
Client identification relies on IP address.
